piezas.titular: Wharton releases Primer, an open system that turns a conversation into a simulation
piezas.entradilla: Wharton Generative AI Labs offers an open-source prototype in which a team of agents interviews the teacher and builds a simulation for students. Its authors warn that it has not been evaluated in classrooms.
cuerpo: Wharton Generative AI Labs, the generative AI lab at the University of Pennsylvania, has presented [Primer](https://gail.wharton.upenn.edu/primer/), a system designed to let teachers create educational simulations without programming. The announcement was shared in EduMedia-IAG.

The process has two phases. In the design phase, an intake agent interviews the teacher, another drafts a design document that the teacher must approve before anything is built, and others generate the characters’ instructions, the images and the final experience. In the running phase, a mentor agent activates students’ prior knowledge and detects misconceptions; a practice agent proposes a role-play or an activity in which the student explains what they have learned; and a feedback agent acts as a coach based on the transcript. After each session, the teacher receives individual and group reports.

Its four design principles are to create through conversation, to leave the teacher in the role of expert, to build learning science into each agent’s instructions, and to publish prompts, templates and code so that they can be inspected and improved.

The page itself describes it as an experimental prototype: it has not been evaluated as a learning intervention in classroom conditions, nor has its compliance with student privacy rules such as FERPA or COPPA been reviewed, and anyone using it with students takes on that review. The page does not name the licence, but [its GitHub repository](https://github.com/wharton-generative-ai-labs/primer) states the MIT licence. There is also a [technical paper](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=7696720), linked from the official page.
piezas.comprobado: Opened Primer’s official page (gail.wharton.upenn.edu/primer): agents in each phase, design approval, reports to the teacher, principles, warnings about the lack of evaluation and about privacy, links to GitHub and SSRN. Opened the GitHub repository: MIT licence (the official page does not name it). The SSRN paper could not be opened (HTTP 403); we only say that the official page links to it. The original tweet could not be opened; the Telegram message only carries its preview. Checked that message 12242 in EduMedia-IAG matches the topic.

piezas.titular: INTEF to present the 2026 update of its AI guide at SIMO on 13 November
piezas.entradilla: According to INTEF’s programme at SIMO EDUCACIÓN, that day was to see the presentation of the new version of its guide on the use of AI in education and another on how to integrate it into schools.
cuerpo: The Spanish National Institute of Educational Technologies and Teacher Training (INTEF) devoted two sessions of its programme at SIMO EDUCACIÓN 2026 (IFEMA Madrid) to artificial intelligence, according to [its announcement](https://intef.es/Noticias/intef-en-simo-2026/), which was shared in ChatGPT-IA-edu.

At 10:30, in room 3, the presentation of the 2026 update of the [Guide on the use of artificial intelligence in education](https://run.gob.es/dra6676f_EN) was scheduled, with attention to AI literacy, privacy and digital wellbeing, and a classroom case. It is version 2.0, published in September, which is also in the ChatGPT-IA-edu [Digital Library](https://t.me/ChatGPTedu/21753/52295). At 13:30, in the same room, came “Guidelines for the integration of artificial intelligence in schools”, a guide to aligning AI with the school’s educational project, built around regulation, literacy and collaboration.
The announcement only gives the programme; the content of the second guide has not been checked.

piezas.titular: ElevenLabs’ Scribe v3 cuts Spanish errors by 35%, according to the company
piezas.entradilla: ElevenLabs’ new speech-to-text models reduce word errors compared with Scribe v2. The figures are the company’s own.
cuerpo: On 10 November ElevenLabs presented on its blog [Scribe v3 and Scribe v3 Live](https://elevenlabs.io/blog/scribe-v3), two speech-to-text models: the first for recorded audio and the second for real-time audio. The news was shared in EduMedia-IAG.

According to the company, Scribe v3 makes 27% fewer word errors than Scribe v2 across 102 languages, and 35% fewer in Spanish. Scribe v3 Live reduces “semantic” word errors by 43% and the standard word error rate by 31% compared with Scribe v2 Realtime, and is the first in the series to identify speakers in real time. In the recorded version, the company reports 12% fewer errors when separating speakers and 17% fewer with three or more. These are ElevenLabs’ own measurements, not those of third parties.

In the classroom it could be useful for transcribing lessons, interviews or student recordings. Both models are available in its API and are the defaults in its app; the article does not mention prices and, by default, processing takes place in the United States, with isolated environments in the EU only for enterprise customers, something to bear in mind with students’ voices.

fuentes.titulo: Introducing Scribe v3 and v3 Live, ElevenLabs

piezas.comprobado: Opened ElevenLabs’ official article (published on 10 November 2026, updated on the 13th): 27% across 102 languages, 35% in Spanish; for Live, 43% in semantic WER and 31% in standard WER (the introduction only quotes the 43%); diarisation 12% and 17% in the recorded model; real-time diarisation for the first time in the series; availability in the API and app; processing in the US by default and the EU only in isolated environments for enterprises. No prices. Classroom use is the newsroom’s inference. Message 12239 in EduMedia-IAG checked.

piezas.titular: Atlas en xogo, a map game in Galician, joins EDUmind’s apps
piezas.entradilla: A new interactive geography app in Galician has been shared in Vibe Coding Educativo. A full description of its game modes could not be checked.
cuerpo: [Atlas en xogo](https://edumind.es/contenido/htmls/Atlas%20en%20xogo.html) is a web app of interactive maps in Galician, with zoom and a 3D view, hosted on the EDUmind site. The footer of that site credits it to Luis Vilela Acuña, who is also the author of Liga de Valores, whose open-source code the paper covered in a brief.

According to the card published by the groups’ bot, it offers maps of relief, coasts, rivers, seas, climates, countries, capitals and drainage basins of Europe and Spain, with several game modes, hints and hidden names, and it saves students’ progress; the interface switches between Galician, Spanish and English and is aimed at Primary, Secondary and Sixth Form (Bachillerato). The page is dynamic and those details could not be checked one by one.
piezas.comprobado: Opened the Atlas en xogo page: title in Galician, 3D label and zoom controls; no author or licence on the page itself. Opened edumind.es: footer “© 2026 EDUmind® — Luis Vilela Acuña”. Modes, maps, languages and progress saving come only from the bot’s card (message 14971) and could not be verified. Liga de Valores is listed as a brief in publicado.txt (no key, hence no link).
piezas.ilustracion_alt: A browser window with a map and the label “Atlas en xogo”; to its left, a magnifying glass with a plus sign, labelled “Zoom”; to its right, a globe labelled “3D view”.
